bills.last_action: Filed; referred to House Rules, Calendar, and Operations — no floor action
bills.summary: 'PFAS Free NC' — would ban knowingly manufacturing, using, or distributing PFAS or PFAS-containing products in North Carolina (except federally required uses), with DEQ civil penalties of $5,000–$25,000 per violation. Also directs NPDES discharge disclosures for PFAS and 1,4-dioxane and technology-based permit limits. The most sweeping PFAS bill filed in the 2025 session; stalled in Rules.
bills.title: PFAS Free NC

bills.last_action: Passed House Agriculture & Environment committee; referred to House Appropriations
bills.summary: 'PFAS Pollution and Polluter Liability' — authorizes the DEQ Secretary to order PFAS manufacturers to pay drinking-water cleanup costs for post-January-2017 discharges and to sue noncompliant firms in superior court. Utilities reimbursed by polluters must refund ratepayers. Bipartisan sponsorship; the legislature's main 'polluter pays' vehicle.
bills.title: PFAS Pollution and Polluter Liability

bills.last_action: Filed; referred to House Rules — no floor action
bills.summary: 'Responsible Firefighting Foam Management Act' — prohibits discharge of PFAS-containing Class B firefighting foam for training, practice, or testing (except legally required testing with containment). Builds on the 2019/2021 AFFF inventory and disposal program run with the NC Collaboratory.
bills.title: Responsible Firefighting Foam Management Act

bills.last_action: Filed; referred to Senate Rules — no floor action (fund concept enacted separately via 2026 budget)
bills.summary: '2026 Water Safety Act' — would create an Emerging Contaminant Mitigation Fund (PFAS + 1,4-dioxane): $56M recurring for local water/wastewater grants, $14M for NC Collaboratory research, plus firefighter-protection funding. The standalone bill stalled, but the 2026 state budget enacted a version of the fund.
bills.title: 2026 Water Safety Act

bills.last_action: Filed; referred to House Rules — no floor action
bills.summary: Exempts menstruation products certified PFAS-free by the Department of Commerce from state sales tax and creates a PFAS product-certification program. A novel product-focused PFAS bill from the 2026 short session; stalled in Rules.
bills.title: Hygiene Products Protections / Sales Tax

bills.last_action: Enacted — signed by Governor Josh Stein
bills.summary: $45M to DEQ for the new Emerging Contaminant Fund (grants to local water systems), $15M to the NC Collaboratory for PFAS remediation at fire stations, $10.2M to the Bernard Allen Emergency Drinking Water Fund for private-well owners, $7M for Collaboratory PFAS research, $3M for DEQ PFAS staffing. A controversial rider makes new Collaboratory studies confidential and exempts its staff from public-records requests — flagged by Clean Cape Fear and SELC.
bills.title: 2026 State Budget — PFAS package

bills.last_action: EMC voted 10–3 to send to public comment (Jan 2026); hearings Apr 2026; pending adoption
bills.summary: EMC PFAS monitoring & minimization rules: industrial dischargers and municipal treatment plants must do baseline PFAS sampling for PFOA, PFOS, and GenX within 60 days, test quarterly for a year, then develop minimization plans. Criticized by SELC as industry-weakened — no numeric discharge limits, after DEQ's stronger 2022 standards proposal was tabled.
bills.title: EMC PFAS Monitoring & Minimization Rules

bills.last_action: Proposed alongside PFAS rules; pending adoption
bills.summary: Companion EMC rule covering 1,4-dioxane — the Cape Fear's other signature contaminant — with the same monitor-then-minimize structure. Same status and same criticisms as the PFAS package.
bills.title: EMC 1,4-Dioxane Monitoring & Minimization Rules

bills.last_action: In effect — initial monitoring results due to the state April 26, 2027
bills.summary: North Carolina incorporated EPA's 2024 federal PFAS drinking-water rule by reference, so community and non-transient non-community water systems must complete initial PFOA/PFOS/GenX/PFHxS/PFNA sampling by April 2027. This is the rule driving utility compliance timelines statewide.
bills.title: NC Drinking-Water PFAS Rule (federal NPDWR incorporated)

bills.id: New Hanover County — Chemours Settlement Water Connection Program
bills.last_action: Board of Commissioners unanimously approved the project ordinance Nov 16, 2026; applications expected early 2027
bills.summary: New Hanover County will invest its $17M share of the Chemours settlement (paid over 10 years) in a public-water connection program for residents on PFAS-contaminated private wells — the first county-level allocation plan surfaced for the $590M settlement. The initial 3-year phase ($5M) covers about 508 properties: 47 adjacent to existing lines at up to $25,000 per connection, and 461 more through 15 CFPUA water-main extension projects at $10,000 per connection. Eligibility requires adjacency to an existing or planned CFPUA main plus documented PFAS in the private well; there is no PFAS-threshold or income restriction. Distinct from the separate March 2026 $17M ECSDC grant to CFPUA — same dollar figure, different funding.
bills.title: New Hanover County Settlement Connection Program

bills.last_action: EPA information-collection notice (FR 2026-23125, Nov 13, 2026) signals EPA intends to finalize the Nov 2025 proposed exemptions as proposed; comments on the notice run through Dec 14, 2026
bills.status: Proposed — signaled for finalization, NOT final
bills.summary: EPA has signaled it will finalize exemptions to the one-time TSCA section 8(a)(7) PFAS reporting rule proposed in November 2025 — including a 0.1% de minimis threshold and carve-outs for imported articles, byproducts, impurities, R&D chemicals, and non-isolated intermediates. EPA's updated burden estimate drops the reporting universe from about 131,411 entities to 255, and expected reports from 67,548 to 1,461. The exemptions are NOT final: the amendments have not yet gone to OMB, and a revised reporting window (3 months, beginning 60 days after a final rule takes effect) would replace the current schedule. If finalized, the exemptions would sharply narrow what EPA ever learns about PFAS in commerce.
bills.title: EPA PFAS Reporting-Rule Exemptions — TSCA 8(a)(7)
